sentences.text: Sinopliosaurus is a dubious genus of pliosauroid plesiosaur, meaning its validity as a distinct group is questioned by scientists.
Fossils once thought to belong to this marine reptile were later identified as teeth from the spinosaurid dinosaur Siamosaurus.
The species Sinopliosaurus weiyuanensis was considered to be a freshwater plesiosaur, a surprising habitat for such a creature.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of three vertebrae and a tooth found in the Lianmugin Formation.
Sinopliosaurus belongs to the order Plesiosauria, the suborder Pliosauroidea, and the family Pliosauridae.
In 2008, researchers reclassified Sinopliosaurus fusuiensis as a spinosaurid relative to Siamosaurus.

Sinopliosaurus lived during the Aptian and Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous in China, though some remains are disputedly dated to the Toarcian age. The recorded time range for Sinopliosaurus spans from the Toarcian to the Tithonian, between 184.2 and 143.1 million years ago.
The status of Sinopliosaurus remains debated because some of its fossils were reassigned to dinosaurs, casting doubt on whether it represents a valid plesiosaur genus.
